SAP Labs Interview Experience 
For 2023 Summer Internship (On-campus) 
Sayali Panch | B.Tech IT [2020-2024 Batch] 
 
SAP Labs India is SAP's largest Research and Development centre outside its 
headquarters in Germany. It has one of the best and most used ERP software 
and cloud computing service in the world. 
 
Eligibility criteria: 70 % or 7 CGPA and above in current graduating degree and 
60% in 10th & 12th 
Job description: 
Any (Developer/QA/Support/DevOps/Dev Support) 
Job location: 
Bangalore/Pune/Mumbai/Gurgaon  
 
Round 1: Online Coding Round 
It was held on 4th August at 11:15 am and was of 45 min duration. It was SHL 
Proctored and had support for all the major languages with IDE. It had 2 easy 
level coding questions for me, but for some other people it had medium level 
questions as well. Switching between questions was allowed. 
Both questions were in a story format with a lot of unnecessary details, so 
choosing what is relevant, i.e., input format, required operations on input and 
output format is important.  
1. An input of space separated numbers was given, you had to return the 
sum of the digits of each number in an array.  
Similar to - https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/program-for-sum-of-the-
digits-of-a-given-number/  just had to be run in a loop for each number. 
 
2. We had to return the count of occurrence of a given word from a 
continuous (no spaces) paragraph with case insensitivity. 
Similar to - https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/frequency-substring-string/   
but had to first convert everything to lowercase. 
I passed all the test cases of both the questions in around 25 min.

Round 2: Technical Interview I 
40 students were selected for this round. It was conducted on Microsoft 
Teams Platform from 9 am onwards on 9th August. It lasted for around 45 min 
for me. 
• First the interviewer introduced himself and then asked me if I was 
nervous and told me to be comfortable. 
• Then he asked me to introduce myself and give a detail description of all 
the projects that I had mentioned in my resume. He asked some counter 
questions on my prior internship project and asked me about my 
experience there. (Refer all your projects mentioned in resume prior to 
the interview as they may cross question in detail) 
• Later he asked me which languages I was familiar with and asked about 
my C++ proficiency. 
• Later he proceeded to ask OOPs questions: 
i. 
Describe the pillars of oops 
ii. 
What is the difference between abstraction and encapsulation, 
show it using a code. [I used C++ to do it, I was told to share my 
screen and use notepad ☹ to do it] 
iii. 
What is the difference between abstract class and interface? 
What happens when you inherit them? Is the child abstract too?  
iv. 
Name the different types of polymorphism and give examples of 
each. [I was asked a lot of counter questions regarding operator 
overloading in python (about magic functions)] 
v. 
Why should we use oops? Give a real-life example. 
• What is the difference between programming and scripting language? 
Give examples of both (while giving the answer I didn’t mention python 
anywhere so he asked me what it was, I said I knew it was interpreter 
based and not complied but not exactly sure what it was) 
• He asked me what cs subjects have been taught (DBMS, OS, DAA etc.). 
Then asked if CN had been taught and I said our 5th semester has just 
started so not really. 
• DAA: 
i. 
Name some sorting algorithms that you know.  
ii. 
What is the time complexity of merge sort. Implement merge sort 
in a code. [Again, I was told to use notepad!] 
iii. 
What is a complete binary tree?

iv. 
What are heaps and its types? 
v. 
You are given an array of 1st ‘n’ numbers but 1 no. among those is 
missing, find the missing no. [I said if it was sorted, we could 
simply use brute force and find it in O(n) or if it wasn’t we could 
find the sum of the given nos. and subtract it from the sum of 1st n 
nos. which we already know (n(n-1)/2) and we will get the missing 
no.] 
vi. 
Implement a linked list [I did it in python] and then he asked some 
standard variations and asked the time complexity of performing 
various operations (inset, delete at various locations) [In Notepad] 
• He asked me to add 2 nos. without using add operator [ I did a-(-b) and 
he seemed satisfied] 
• He asked me this puzzle:  
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-27-hourglasses-puzzle/ 
• He asked me if I had any questions for him and I asked him one. 
 
Round 3: Technical Interview II 
30 students were selected for this round. It was conducted on Microsoft 
Teams Platform on the same day post lunch. It lasted for around 40 min for 
me. 
• I was again asked to introduce myself and describe all my projects. 
(There were no cross questions this time) 
• OOPs: 
i. 
Which type of inheritance is not allowed in Java and why? 
(Multiple inheritance; I gave the famous diamond problem as the 
reason) How can we still implement this if needed? 
• OS: 
i. 
What do you understand by the term OS and give some examples 
of it. 
ii. 
What is the difference between threads and processes? 
iii. 
What is multithreading? 
iv. 
What is Virtual Memory? (Asked a lot of sub questions like what 
are pages, frames, different page replacement algorithms) 
v. 
What is thrashing? 
vi. 
What are semaphores? Why are they used?

vii. 
What is deadlock and what are the conditions for it to occur? 
• DBMS: 
i. 
What are ACID properties, explain each in detail. 
ii. 
What is normalization? Why is it necessary?  
iii. 
What are some TCL commands and explain their implementation. 
• She asked me 2 puzzles: 
i. 
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-36-matchstick-
puzzle/?ref=lbp 
ii. 
https://www.chrisnewland.com/logic-puzzle-buckets-of-water-4l-
7l-make-5l-135  For this she asked me if I could give a pseudo code 
to generalise the question. Refer this for solution: 
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/two-water-jug-
puzzle/#:~:text=Solution%201%20(Always%20pour%20from,conta
ins%20d%20litres%20of%20water. 
 
Round 4: HR Interview  
9 students were selected for this round. It was conducted on Microsoft Teams 
Platform again on the same day in the evening. It was about 5-10 min long. All 
the students selected for this round were selected for the internship. 
It was a very relaxed round; the interviewer was very friendly and just asked 
about my hobbies and interests and what made me interested in studying IT.  
She asked me about my family background and schooling years. Any specific 
achievements I wanted to highlight. Then she asked me if I had any location 
which I would not be comfortable going to for internship.  
Finally, she asked me if I had any questions for her (again I asked her one). 
 
Resources used: 
• DSA: Geek for Geeks, Love Babbar 450 DSA cracker, Aditya Verma 
Playlist (for DP) 
• OS: Gate Smashers Playlist, Geek for Geeks, Love Babbar sheet  
• OOPS: Love Babbar sheet, InterviewBit 
• DBMS: Love Babbar sheet, InterviewBit 
• Puzzles: Geek for Geeks

Tips: 
• While preparing, stick to one/few resources. There are many good 
resources out there but if you juggle too much you may miss some 
concepts. 
• While answering be confident, trust your instincts, explain your thought 
process and keep continuously interacting. 
• Do not lie on your resume, interviewers ask a lot of questions based on 
it. 
• Rather than assuming, it is always better to ask the interviewers to 
repeat/explain the question again. 
• In coding questions/puzzles the interviewer wants to check your 
approach to solve the problem so don’t worry too much if you forget the 
syntax.  
• If you don’t know or are not sure about something, say so rather than 
wasting time or making random guesses; the interviewers usually help or 
give hints to you. (No one expects you to know everything) 
• Prepare a short introduction ready so that you do not miss out anything 
during the interview (Almost every interviewer asks to give one) 
• Research about the company and keep at least 2-3 good questions 
ready, so when the interviewer asks if you have any questions for them 
you are prepared. 
 
Most of the interview rounds are kept on the same day and the 
schedule/result announcement is very erratic. So, make sure to stay 
hydrated and eat in between. 
 
 
All the best!!
